title: Pre-Analysis — Oxygen Transducer Standard Against a Composite Cylinder Proposal
abstract: Closed work order testing whether the solid-state transducer standard would survive a change of cylinder material, raised against an operator weight-saving proposal and closed with the proposal rejected.

sections.objective: Establish what the solid-state pressure transducer standard assumes about the cylinder it is fitted to, in support of an operator proposal to substitute a lighter composite cylinder on the four-engine fleet. The specific question was whether the transducer, the cradle and the indicating channel would still be valid if the cylinder changed.
sections.findings_summary: The transducer itself is indifferent to the cylinder material; it reads pressure at the outlet and nothing in its calibration depends on what the pressure is contained in. The cradle is not indifferent. The moulded saddle introduced with this standard is dimensioned to the steel cylinder neck and would not fit a composite one, and the strap tension is set for a body that does not creep. Two further findings were more significant than the hardware. The composite cylinder carries a fifteen year service life against the twenty-five year life of the steel item, which converts a life-of-aircraft part into a scheduled replacement and reverses the whole-life cost case. And the removal task assumes a cylinder that can be carried by two people with a strap around the body, which a composite item can be but with different handling instructions. The proposal failed on the service life rather than on anything found here.
sections.next_steps: Report that the transducer standard does not obstruct the proposal but the cradle does, and that the service life is the decisive point. Offer the operator the lightweight cradle already released for the twin-engine fleet as a partial answer. Take no action on the transducer, the servicing task or the indicating channel.

Check the cradle and saddle geometry against a composite body

evidence.similarity_note: The order and this work order describe the same proposal in entirely different registers, one commercial and one engineering, and share no identifier.

expected_findings.rationale: The internal order sets out the weight case and the launch customer offer. The engineering position developed here is the answer to it, and the two need to be traceable to each other so that a later request on the same subject finds the reasoning rather than repeating it.
expected_findings.resolution: Record this work order as the engineering basis for the order closure note.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the non-return valve and charging pump part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task instructs a lifting strap around the cylinder body and a strap release sequence dimensioned to the steel cradle. Both would need restating for a composite cylinder.
expected_findings.resolution: No action; recorded against the proposal rather than the task.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity between the dispatch pressure discussion and the proposal text; no identifier is shared and the two documents are written for different audiences.

expected_findings.rationale: The crew limitation is expressed as a dispatch table entered with pressure and cylinder temperature. A composite cylinder has a different temperature response and the table would have to be recomputed, which nobody had costed.
expected_findings.resolution: No action; recorded as a further reason the proposal was not free.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The proposal is rejected on service life and cradle geometry; the transducer standard is unaffected.
